programs.title: CHINA-GERMANY BUSINESS TIES AI and robotics become increasingly important in workplace
programs.desc: The German Chamber of Commerce in China has released its latest Labor Market and Salary Report, which indicates that German companies operating in China anticipate an average salary increase of 3.19% in 2026. CGTN reporter Yu Bokun interviewed Oliver Oehms, Executive Director and Board Member of the German Chamber of Commerce in China – North China, to discuss the labor market outlook and the evolving innovation landscape in China—particularly the growing trend of knowledge and technology transfer from Chinese branches back to German headquarters.

programs.title: What can Africa learn from China’s poverty reduction experience?
programs.desc: Five years after China eliminated absolute poverty, its development experience continues to attract attention around the world, particularly across Africa. What lessons can African countries draw from China’s journey? Can China’s poverty reduction experiences be adapted to African realities? In today’s episode, we bring scholars, journalists and development practitioners from China, The Gambia, Rwanda and Namibia. Jainaba Sonko, Zhang Yanqiu, Patrick Rurangangabo and Jeronimo Kateya explore pathways to sustainable development and poverty reduction, discussing governance, infrastructure, education, self-reliance and the future of China-Africa cooperation.

programs.title: KOLs and other ways to connect cultures
programs.desc: In what ways can KOLs better use their power in an age where a single video can reach millions? Tune in to #GlobalSouthNextGen: Voices and Visions, and check out the stories of two KOLs from Ghana and Indonesia who use their creativity, empathy, and the shared desire to make people understand each other a little better.

programs.title: KOL traffic secrets: the power to drive change #GlobalSouthNextGen Behind the scenes
programs.desc: How do creators build traffic on social media? How can that influence spark real changes in society? In a cozy siheyuan, the iconic Beijing courtyard, another episode of #GlobalSouthNextGen: Voices and Visions brings together two KOLs who open up about their journeys, their strategies, and the impact from their content. Click into the Behind the Scenes video to find out more!

programs.title: Start small, dream big: Young entrepreneurs shape our future
programs.desc: Tune in to #GlobalSouthNextGen: Voices and Visions! Hear the incredible stories of the young entrepreneurs who are doing things differently. One connects beauty services with people in need, while the other turns waste into sustainable solutions, all while lifting up their communities. Don’t you miss this!

programs.title: Startup Secrets & Backstage Gossip! #GlobalSouthNextGen Behind the scenes
programs.desc: Ever thought of turning human hair waste into sustainable products? How can young people take their first step in initiating their own business? At Suzhou Pingjiang Cultural Center, another episode of #GlobalSouthNextGen: Voices and Visions invites two young entrepreneurs to share their amazing stories. Click into the BehindTheScenes video to find out more!

programs.title: How the SCO opens doors for young entrepreneurs
programs.desc: Expanding practical cooperation within the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) is nurturing new industries and development opportunities across Central Asia. CGTN speaks with Victoria Khu, co-founder of the SCOLAR Network, and Ulan Abdurazakov, CEO of Nineninesix.ai, to discuss how SCO cooperation shapes young people's education and career paths.

programs.title: Zhejiang transforms technology into market success
programs.desc: East China's Zhejiang Province has long been known for its strong private-sector economy and vibrant business environment. Now, it's putting that market-driven approach to work in next-generation technology, helping turn lab innovations into real-world products. CGTN reporter Wang Tianyu reports from Zhejiang.

programs.title: The village workshops giving rural residents a new choice in Zhejiang
programs.desc: For millions of Chinese workers, earning more has often meant leaving home. But one village in Zhejiang is trying to change that. A local workshop is bringing jobs closer to home. CGTN reporter Yu Bokun sees how it is creating new opportunities.

programs.title: How China turns humble loofah plants into premium bath products
programs.desc: A simple loofah can become a premium bath or kitchen product worth more than $10. Behind that transformation is a partnership between Huangmei in Hubei and Ningbo — one provides the land and labor, the other the technology and markets. CGTN's Yu Bokun finds out how this humble crop goes global.

programs.title: RAZOR: Glacier Collapse
programs.desc: Glaciers worldwide are melting, collapsing, and vanishing faster than ever before. On August 26th, a massive glacier collapse on the China-Nepal border triggered catastrophic flash floods and mudslides, sweeping through villages and leaving hundreds dead and thousands missing. These events are a stark reminder of how a warming planet is reshaping some of the world’s most fragile mountain environments. RAZOR's Reya El-Salahi travels to Switzerland, where the Bircher Glacier's collapse in 2025 buried the village of Blatten beneath millions of tons of ice and rock. Professor Daniel Farinotti and a team of researchers from ETH Zurich and WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF are analysing what happened to help predict the outcome of future collapses.

programs.title: RAZOR: Coral Babies
programs.desc: The race to save the world's coral is on. These vital organisms are being devastated by mass bleaching events caused by climate change. At current rates, 99% could perish in marine heatwaves by the 2030s. To help ensure their survival, scientists are urgently working to reproduce coral species and restore reefs. RAZOR's Reya El-Salahi visits the landlocked University of Derby—75 miles from the sea—where Dr Michael Sweet and his team are pioneering coral breeding techniques. By replicating reef conditions and even mimicking lunar cycles, they've successfully induced coral spawning—an event rarely seen by humans.

programs.title: Razor: Vanishing Snow
programs.desc: In this episode of Razor, RAZOR's Gabrielle Lawrence travels to the Italian Alps to investigate how climate change is causing snow to disappear at an alarming rate. At the Angelo Mosso Institute, scientists like Michele Freppaz and Luigi Perotti reveal how shrinking snowpack is reshaping ecosystems, increasing avalanche risks, and accelerating glacier retreat. Using cutting-edge tools and long-term data, researchers uncover how these changes threaten water supplies, mountain communities, and entire industries. This is not just a story about melting snow—it’s a race to understand and protect one of Earth’s most fragile environments.

programs.title: The Takaichi Fallout-Behind Japan's Yen Crisis
programs.desc: The yen has plunged to multi-decade lows, prompting a rare coordinated currency intervention by Japan and the United States. Meanwhile, U.S. Treasury yields are surging, with the 30-year yield reaching its highest level since 2007.What is driving the yen’s weakness？Is Japan’s yen crisis becoming a global bond-market story? Join us on BizTalk as we examine Japan’s economic challenges, #TheTakaichiFallout and the global risks behind the latest bond-market sell-off.

programs.title: Computing Art: Breaking boundaries with digital art-计算机艺术 用数字艺术打破边界
programs.desc: Artists have been using algorithms to create art for decades. But over the years, they have pushed the boundaries with computing art. For many artists today, data has become their paintbrush, changing the way we experience art.

programs.title: New life for world cultural heritage
programs.desc: A sad day for humanity as a massive fire spread throughout Paris' Notre-Dame Cathedral on Monday. The blaze gulf the building's spire and roof to collapse. The Paris landmark has seen numerous restorations in its 800-plus-year history, but this time, a rebuild is needed, as pledged by France President Emmanuel Macron. But how? The only news not that bad today is that for years, architectural historians worked with laser scanners to capture the entirety of the cathedral's interior and exterior in meticulous 3D point clouds, a technology called 3D mapping. In season 2 of CGTN's original series Tech It Out, we reported this technology used by scientists to protect fragile world heritage in China. We hope this will make your day a little bit easier.

programs.title: How flexible can this futuristic screen be?
programs.desc: Display technology has been revolutionized in the past few decades. Images are sharper, and colors look clearer. Despite these improvements, displays are essentially the same as they were decades ago: They’re flat, rigid pieces of glass. Boring, isn’t it? Recently we have got more choices. You probably own a mobile phone or even TV with a curved display, but what’s more exciting is bendable screen. This year, Chinese display manufacture BOE has announced to start mass production of flexible AMOLED screens in Sichuan Province. They will rival Samsung in this market. See, flexible screens are next big thing.

programs.title: FPV, the future racing
programs.desc: First-person-view (FPV) drone racing, the art of flying drones around obstacle courses at incredible speeds (180 to 200 Kilometers per hour) and using head-mounted displays and joysticks to control their direction, has started to emerge as a new sport in China. Since the first race began in China, FPV has attracted a loyal fan base, among them are a number of professional pilots who intend to turn this novelty concept into a mainstream sport.

programs.title: Meet China: Starting Green, Reaching the Future
programs.desc: In this episode of Meet China, wind becomes more than a natural force—it powers a greener future across China and Europe. A piece of fabric reveals how Chinese innovation is reshaping global perceptions of manufacturing. Ancient ruins in central China are reimagined as immersive cultural experiences, turning heritage into living memory. And in Laos, Chinese agricultural expertise is helping farmers unlock higher yields and new opportunities. From energy and textiles to tourism and farming, this episode shows how innovation is renewing tradition and connecting futures across borders.

programs.title: Beyond the screen: how “film ” tourism and AI redefine moviegoer experience
programs.desc: As the Beijing International Film Festival takes over the city, films are no longer just something we watch in cinemas. They’re connecting tourism, retail, entertainment, and even cutting-edge tech. What does this “film plus” experience look like for audiences today? And as AI reshapes the film industry, what opportunities and challenges lie ahead? Host Xu Yawen spoke with Li Lun, assistant professor of economics at Peking University; Geng Ling, film producer and CEO of China Film Assist Company; and Teng Jimeng, associate professor of American studies at Beijing Foreign Studies University, to delve into these questions.

programs.desc: CGTN reporter Li Jianhua reports on how Londoners live without air conditioning, despite the British summers getting longer and heater.

programs.title: Observing Europe-So many UK Prime Ministers, same old problems
programs.desc: Since moving to London, CGTN's Li Jianhua has witnessed the UK cycle through four leaders. In this video, Jianhua reflects on the problems facing each of those prime ministers… and why it's affected how he buys grapes.

programs.title: Observing Europe-Who owns Britain?
programs.desc: One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely. It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners. For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned. In this latest episode of his series Observing Europe, Jianhua explores ownership, investment – and where Britain is drawing the line.

programs.title: Observing Europe - Is migration "weaponized" in Europe?
programs.desc: Schengen - one of Europe’s greatest achievements - is being tested. The Schengen Area promised border-free travel across much of Europe. But migration, security concerns and increasingly polarized politics are putting that promise under pressure. From Ceuta to the return of internal border checks, CGTN Europe correspondent Li Jianhua looks at how Europe’s migration debate is reshaping Schengen — and asks: Can Europe keep its internal borders open as political pressure to control migration grows?
